claim: The library section names 2142:11082 'Tree row' as 'the set every editor board instances' — a 280x28 COMPONENT_SET with a Depth 0-5 x State rest/selected axis, 387 instances file-wide.
truth: The Layers module does not instance it. Every Tree row instance on the Layers boards points at a DIFFERENT master, COMPONENT 243:6 'Tree row' on page '🧩 Components' (1:2), which has 57 instances file-wide and no Depth axis at all. The two masters are also opposites: 2142:11082 has depth but draws ONLY a text label (one TEXT 'body', paddingLeft 16/32/48/64/80/96, gap 8 — no chevron, no icon, no eye, no lock); 243:6 has all five parts (tint-bg, active bar, chevron, icon, label, eye, lock) and no depth. The brief's premise 'the shared Row component carries no depth axis' is true of 243:6 and FALSE of 2142:11082.
evidence: Measured via scripts/baseline/figma-mcp.mjs use_figma: getNodeByIdAsync('2142:11082') -> COMPONENT_SET props=["Depth","State"], 12 variants, each one TEXT child; getNodeByIdAsync('243:6') -> COMPONENT 280x28 layoutMode=HORIZONTAL props=["Chevron#243:0","Selected#243:1","Glyph#1325:0"], children tint-bg 243:7, active bar 243:8, TEXT '▾' 243:10 @12, FRAME icon 243:11 @22, TEXT 'Layer' 243:12 @40, TEXT '👁' 243:13 @246, TEXT '🔒' 243:14 @262. Instance census over figma.root.findAllWithCriteria({types:['INSTANCE']}) (5749 instances): mainComponent.id==='243:6' -> 57; mainComponent in the twelve 2142:11082 variant ids -> 387. Board 142:2's eight rows (244:1580, 244:1589, 244:1598, 244:1607, 244:1616, 244:1625, 244:1634, 244:1643) all report mainId=243:6.
edit: Settle on ONE Tree row master before any other Layers board edit lands. Recommended: keep 2142:11082 as the shared set (it is the one in the shared-chrome section and has 387 consumers), and port 243:6's five parts into it as component properties on every Depth variant — Chevron (bool, must RESERVE its slot when false, see FIG-I-03), Glyph (instance swap, 12x12), Name (text), Badge (bool, 12px), Eye (bool-state), Lock (bool-state) — then re-point the 57 instances of 243:6 (all Layers boards) at the merged set and delete 243:6. Do NOT do the reverse (adding a Depth axis to 243:6) — it would leave the 387 existing consumers on the label-only row.

claim: 'Layers · tree' is the module's canonical board and draws eight rows: Section, Container, Heading, Button, Gallery, Grid, a-very-long-layer-name-that-truncates, Footer.
truth: All eight rows are at DEPTH 0 — the board draws a flat list, not a tree. The x differences between rows (chevron@12/icon@22/label@40 vs icon@12/label@30) are the 243:6 Chevron boolean removing itself from the auto-layout, not indentation. The product never renders a flat tree: buildLayersFromEngine always emits the page ROOT as row 0 and recurses with depth+1, and the row's left gutter is paddingLeft = 12 + depth*16.
evidence: Fetched 142:2 child geometry: 244:1580 chev@12 icon@22 label@40 'Section'; 244:1598 icon@12 label@30 'Heading'; 244:1607 icon@12 label@30 'Button'; 244:1634 icon@12 label@30 (long name); every row starts its content in the 12-22 band, i.e. one indent level. Code: useLayerTree.ts:88-97 buildTree(rootElement, 0) with children.map(child => buildTree(child, depth+1)) and setLayers([buildTree(rootElement,0)]); LayerTreeItem.tsx:123-125 rowStyle paddingLeft = `${12 + layer.depth * 16}px`, pinned by __tests__/LayerTreeItem.indent.test.tsx.
edit: Re-lay 142:2's rows on the real ladder: row 0 = the page root at depth 0 (chevron@12), its children at depth 1 (chevron@28), grandchildren at depth 2 (chevron@44). 1082:4640 already draws the correct ladder (12/28/44/60/76) — copy its row geometry onto 142:2 and onto the six sibling 143-family boards, which repeat the same flat list.

claim: A leaf row (no children) is drawn with its type icon in the chevron's slot: on 1082:4640 the depth-4 leaf 'Logo' has icon@76 while its depth-4 parent sibling 'Nav' has chevron@76 and icon@86; on 1082:4835 every depth-1 leaf has icon@28 while depth-0 parents have chevron@12 icon@22.
truth: The product RESERVES the chevron slot on leaf rows, so a leaf's icon lines up with its siblings' icons rather than sliding 10px left. The chevron button is always rendered and only its visibility is dropped.
evidence: layers-v2.css:73 `.bdc-lr.bdc-leaf .bdc-lr-chev { visibility: hidden; }` — visibility, not display, so the 12x12 box (layers-v2.css:58-60) keeps its space. LayerTreeItem.tsx:200-214 renders the chevron Button unconditionally, adding class 'bdc-leaf' at :134 when children.length===0. Figma side: 243:6 is layoutMode=HORIZONTAL, so the Chevron boolean REMOVES the node from the flow and the row re-packs — measured on 142:2, where turning it off moves icon 22->12 and label 40->30.
edit: On master 243:6 (or its merged successor, FIG-I-01): make Chevron a visibility toggle that keeps the 4px glyph box + 6px gap in the layout — either swap the boolean for a 2-variant Chevron=shown/hidden where the hidden variant holds a transparent glyph, or add a fixed 10px spacer frame that the boolean does not remove. Then reset the leaf rows on 142:2, 143:60, 1082:4640, 1082:4739 and 1082:4835 so leaf icons align with their siblings'.

claim: The row's internal ladder on every Layers board is: chevron glyph 4px wide at 12+16*depth, icon 12x12 six px later, label eighteen px after that, then bare 10px 👁 and 🔒 glyphs at 246 and 262.
truth: The chevron LADDER matches the product exactly (12 + depth*16) and everything after it does not. The product's chevron is a 12x12 button, the gap is the 8px token, and the trailing pair are 20x20 hit boxes right-anchored to a 6px right padding. Net: every label on every board sits 12px left of where the product puts it, and every icon 10px left.
evidence: Code: LayerTreeItem.tsx:124 paddingLeft 12+depth*16; layers-v2.css:17-33 `.bdc-lr { display:flex; gap: var(--bk-space-8); height:28px; padding: 0 8px }` with --bk-space-8: 8px (tokens.generated.css:102); layers-v2.css:58-60 chevron 12x12; :75-77 icon 12x12; :160-167 `.bdc-lr .bdc-lr-eye, .bdc-lr .bdc-lr-lock { height: 20px }` with an 11px glyph at :176-182; :243-245 `.bdc-layers-tree-compact .bdc-lr { padding: 2px 6px }` and compact is the shipped default (useLayersState.ts:43). So icon x = paddingLeft+20, label x = paddingLeft+40, lock box 254-274, eye box 226-246. Board (fetched 1082:4640): depth-0 row 1082:4649 chev@12 icon@22 label@40 eye@246 lock@262.

At depth 0 that puts icon@32, label@52, eye box 226-246, lock box 254-274. Apply once on the master (FIG-I-01) rather than per board.

claim: Caption 155:25 reads: '28h dense rows. At depth 5 the name gets 120px: 288 − 80 indent − 16 chevron − 16 icon − 8 gap − 48 for the two toggles. The long row here is the stress case.'
truth: Only the row height is right. The panel is 280 wide, not 288; the depth-5 indent is 92, not 80; the chevron and icon are 12 each, not 16; there are FOUR 8px gaps, not one; the two toggles are 20 each = 40, not 48; and the name therefore gets 86px, not 120. Formula: name = 280 − (12+16d) − 6 − 12 − 12 − 20 − 20 − 32 = 166 − 16d.
evidence: --bk-size-drawer: 280px (themes/tokens.generated.css:129), read by LeftSidebar.css:231 `width: var(--drawer-w, var(--bk-size-drawer))`; shared/constants/layout.ts:20-36 records that this token is the one the shipping drawer reads. Indent 12+16*5=92 (LayerTreeItem.tsx:124). Chevron 12x12 (layers-v2.css:58-60), icon 12x12 (:75-77), eye/lock height 20 (:160-167), gap var(--bk-space-8)=8px (:20 + tokens.generated.css:102), compact right padding 6 (:243-245, default per useLayersState.ts:43).
edit: Replace the caption text on 155:25 with: '28h dense rows. At depth 5 the name gets 86px: 280 − 92 indent − 12 chevron − 12 icon − 4×8 gaps − 40 for the two toggles − 6 right pad. The long row here is the stress case.'

claim: Caption 155:26 reads: 'Only matching nodes, ancestors kept so the path still reads.'
truth: Ancestors are NOT kept. The filter does build an ancestor-preserving tree, and then the panel throws it away: it walks that tree and pushes only the rows that themselves match, each rewritten to `children: [], depth: 0`. The rendered result is a flat list of matches with no indentation, no chevrons and no ancestor context. The path is recoverable only from the breadcrumb after you click a result.
evidence: index.tsx:346-359 — `if (!state.searchHook.isSearching) return treeFiltered;` then `walk` pushes `{...it, children: [], depth: 0}` for each `itemMatches(...)` and returns `flat`; the comment above it at :343-345 states the intent ('search results render FLAT — only the matching rows, no indentation, no chevrons, no ancestor context'). The ancestor-keeping filter it discards is useLayerSearch.ts:27-40 filterTreeItems.
edit: Replace 155:26's text with: 'Only matching rows, rendered flat — no indent, no chevrons. Ancestors are dropped; the breadcrumb above the tree is how the path comes back.' Then redraw 143:2's single result row at depth 0 with no chevron, and populate the breadcrumb band above it.

claim: Caption 155:28 reads: 'Refused with the reason, and no line — the absence of the line is half the message.'
truth: The line IS drawn over an illegal target, right up to the moment of the drop. Legality is not consulted while dragging: handleDragOver derives before/after/inside from pointer geometry alone and sets dragState, which is what paints the 2px line. The nesting rules (canNestElement / canHaveChildren / locked-parent) are only evaluated inside handleLayerDrop, i.e. after the user has already let go. So the user sees an accepting cue, drops, and then gets a refusal alert at the top of the panel.
evidence: index.tsx:238-270 handleDragOver — computes `position` from `y < height*0.3` / `> 0.7` / container-middle and calls `state.setDragState(...)` with no legality check; layers-v2.css:196-212 paints the line from `[data-drop="before"|"after"]` and the inset ring from `[data-drop="inside"]`. The four refusals all live in handleLayerDrop: index.tsx:124-127 locked container, :130-133 `${parentType} cannot contain children`, :134-137 `${sourceType} cannot be nested inside ${parentType}`, :144-147 locked parent, :150-153 `${sourceType} cannot be placed in ${parentType}` — each calling showDropError, which renders the top-of-panel alert at :399-404 and self-clears after 3s (:90-95).
edit: Replace 155:28's text with: 'The line is drawn over illegal targets too — the drop is what refuses, not the hover. The reason appears as an alert at the top of the panel and clears itself after 3s.' Keep 143:119's missing line only if the design intends to ADD a pre-drop legality check; if so, say so on the caption and file it as a product change, because today the board describes behaviour the panel does not have.

claim: A 280x812 board named 'Layers · list-view' sits in the section, already self-labelled UNBUILDABLE in the manifest.
truth: Confirmed: there is no list view, no view-mode switch and no state to hold one anywhere in the module. The panel renders exactly one presentation — a role="tree" of LayerTreeItem rows — and the only presentation preference that exists is treeDensity comfortable|compact.
evidence: `grep -rni 'list-view|listView|viewMode' editor/panels/layers editor/sidebar/tabs/layers` -> zero hits (run 2026-09-06). The full preference model is LayerDisplayPrefs = { showHtmlBadges, showElementIds, treeDensity } (types.ts:60-67); the only renderer is index.tsx:424-475 (`role="tree"`, one branch). No toolbar control other than ⊞ / ⊟ / ⚙ exists (LayersTab.tsx:176-184).
edit: Rename 1082:5004 to 'NOT IMPLEMENTED — no list view exists; the panel has one presentation and only a density preference'. Do not delete the frame. Add a caption frame beside it (clone 155:32, 280x18) reading 'Never built. The only display preference the panel has is Compact rows (LayerDisplayPrefs.treeDensity).'

claim: 1082:4739 draws two badge glyphs at x=229: a filled ◆ on Button, Icon button and Card, and a hollow ◇ on Badge, Nav bar, Nav item 1/2/3, CTA button and Input field — and it badges a whole subtree (Nav bar plus all three of its children).
truth: Two things the product cannot do. (1) Only ONE badge exists: the hollow ◇, gated on ComponentManager.isInstance. There is no master badge — it needs a persisted master↔element link the model does not carry, which the code says in so many words. (2) isInstance is a registry membership test keyed by the instance ROOT's element id, so at most one row in a Nav-bar subtree can carry it; the code deliberately removed the descendant-wide signal because no board drew it — while this board draws exactly that.
evidence: LayerTreeItem.tsx:115 `const isInstance = !!composer?.components?.isInstance?.(layer.id);` rendering a single `\u25C7` at :256-264; the comment at :101-114 records both facts ('Only the INSTANCE link (◇) exists in the registry today — the board's ◆ master badge needs a persisted master↔element link the model doesn't carry yet' and 'the descendant signal is not on any board and is gone with it'). ComponentManager.ts:444-446 `isInstance(elementId) { return this.instances.has(elementId); }` — a Map keyed by the instance root's element id (:435-442 getInstance). Fetched rows: 1082:4754 '◆'@229, 1082:4766 Card '◆'@229, 1082:4789 Nav bar '◇'@229 with children 1082:4796/4802/4808 each '◇'@229.

Also re-anchor the badge: the code places it inline immediately after the name (flex-shrink 0, layers-v2.css:148-153), not pinned at a fixed x=229.

claim: The popover draws four options: 'Show hidden layers' ON, 'Show lock badges' ON, 'Compact rows' OFF, 'Highlight CMS-bound' OFF (per W-M-13, which I am citing rather than re-fetching).
truth: W-M-13 already settled that only one of the four options exists. The fact it did not record is that the one shared option is drawn in the WRONG state: Compact rows ships ON by default, by explicit founder call, and the panel's tree carries the compact class on first paint. The board draws the density the product does not use.
evidence: useLayersState.ts:33-44 defaultPrefs = { showHtmlBadges: false, showElementIds: false, treeDensity: 'compact' } with the founder call recorded inline ('Compact by default — founder call, 2026-08-28'); index.tsx:427 appends ' bdc-layers-tree-compact' whenever treeDensity==='compact'; layers-v2.css:243-245 gives that class `padding: 2px 6px`. Stored prefs are spread over the defaults (useLayersState.ts:46-54), so ON is the state a first-time user sees. Prior finding: W-M-13 (option set, popover width, missing close control).

claim: Every Layers board labels its rows with element TYPE names — Section, Container, Heading, Button, Gallery, Grid, Footer, Page, Hero, Nav, Link 1/2/3, CTA button.
truth: The type label is the LAST branch the product takes, not the first. A row shows, in order: the user's custom name; otherwise, for text-ish elements, the first 32 characters of the element's own copy; otherwise the type label. Eight of the twelve types on these boards are in the previewable set, so on a real page most of these rows would read as sentences — 'Build your site in minutes', 'Get started free' — not as 'Heading' and 'Button'. This is shape, not sample data: the board teaches the reader that the tree is a list of type names, and it is not.
evidence: data/layerUtils.ts:69-79 getDisplayName — `const custom = customNames.get(id); if (custom) return custom; if (preview) return preview; return ELEMENT_TYPE_LABELS[type] ?? …`, with the drift history in the comment at :63-68. useLayerTree.ts:78-86 PREVIEWABLE = text, heading, paragraph, button, link, label, quote, list-item; previewOf strips tags, collapses whitespace and truncates at 32 with an ellipsis. LayerTreeItem.tsx:98 calls getDisplayName(layer.id, layer.type, customNames, layer.preview).
edit: On 142:2 and its siblings, relabel the text-ish rows with copy and keep type labels only for containers: e.g. row 244:1598 'Heading' -> 'Build your site in minutes', row 244:1607 'Button' -> 'Get started free', and keep 'Section' / 'Container' / 'Grid' / 'Footer' as they are. Keep row 244:1634's long name as the truncation stress case. Add one line to caption 155:25: 'A row shows a custom name, else the element's own first 32 characters, else the type label.'

target: 1776:8375 / 143:179  (Layers · hidden) — new board cloned from it
claim: 143:179 draws hiding as one faded row ('Gallery'), and caption 155:29 says 'Hidden is not deleted. 45% opacity, keeps its place in the tree.'
truth: The caption is right about the row and silent about the consequence: hiding a PARENT dims its whole subtree on canvas while dimming exactly one row in the tree. hiddenIds is a flat Set with no descendant walk, so the child rows stay at full opacity and keep their eyes in the 'not hidden' state — while on canvas the parent's opacity .25 and pointer-events:none apply to everything inside it. A user hides a section, sees one grey row, and finds twelve elements unclickable on canvas with nothing in the tree explaining why.
evidence: useLayerActions.ts:127-137 toggleVisibility adds/removes a single id in hiddenIds; :140-146 sets `data-hidden` on that one DOM node only. LayerTreeItem.tsx:88 `const isHidden = hiddenIds.has(layer.id)` — per row, no ancestor test; layers-v2.css:56 `.bdc-lr.bdc-hidden { opacity: 0.45 }`. Canvas.css:259-262 `[data-buildrick-id][data-hidden="true"] { opacity: .25; pointer-events: none }` — inherited by the whole subtree.
edit: Clone 143:179 as 'Layers · hidden parent'. Draw a container row hidden (0.45, slashed eye) with three expanded children at FULL opacity and open eyes, and a caption (clone 155:29, 280x36): 'Hiding a container dims everything inside it on canvas — pointer-events off — but only the container's own row dims in the tree. Its children keep their eyes open.' Then decide whether the product should dim descendant rows; the board is currently silent either way.

target: 1776:8375 / 1082:4640  (Layers · expanded) — new board cloned from it
claim: The deepest tree anywhere in the section is 1082:4640, which reaches depth 5 (chevrons at 12/28/44/60/76, leaf icons at 92), and the shared row set 2142:11082 caps its Depth axis at 5.
truth: The product's tree is unbounded — buildTree recurses with no depth limit — and the row's name column shrinks by 16px per level, so it runs out. name = 166 − 16*depth: 86px at depth 5, 38px at depth 8, 6px at depth 10, and nothing at depth 11. A Grid inside a Card inside a Column inside a Section inside a Container inside the page root is depth 6 on an ordinary marketing page.
evidence: useLayerTree.ts:88-95 buildTree recurses `element.getChildren().map(child => buildTree(child, depth + 1))` with no cap; LayerTreeItem.tsx:124 paddingLeft 12+depth*16 and :347-349 recurses into children; layers-v2.css:102-107 `.bdc-lr-nm { flex: 1; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis }` — the name is the only flexible child, so it absorbs the whole loss. Row budget per FIG-I-05. Figma: 2142:11082 variants stop at Depth=5 (paddingLeft 96); fetched 1082:4640 leaf icons top out at 92.
edit: Add 'Layers · deep tree' cloned from 1082:4640: same panel, a chain reaching depth 8 with the name column at 38px and ellipsis on every deep row, plus the horizontal-scroll or truncation decision made visible. Add a caption (clone 155:25's 280x72): 'The tree has no depth limit. Every level costs the name 16px — 86px at depth 5, 38px at depth 8, nothing at depth 11. Decide here whether deep rows truncate, wrap, or scroll.' Extend 2142:11082's Depth axis past 5 (or define what a Depth>5 instance uses) in the same pass as FIG-I-01.

claim: No board in the section draws a keyboard-focused row, and no caption states the tree's keyboard contract.
truth: Every row is tabbable and has a distinct focus ring the boards never show — and the contract behind it is unusual enough that it has to be drawn. (a) Arrow keys SELECT rather than move focus, and focus is never moved by the handler, so pressing ArrowDown twice from a row selects the same neighbour twice. (b) Enter/Space select, F2 renames (refused when locked), ArrowRight/Left expand/collapse. (c) Delete does nothing: the global keybinding for delete is bare 'Backspace', and CommandCenter suppresses every bare-key command whose target sits inside a role="tree" — which the whole panel is. Right-click is the only delete path from the tree.
evidence: LayerTreeItem.tsx:172 tabIndex={0}; layers-v2.css:216-220 `.bdc-lr:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--bk-accent); outline-offset: -2px; z-index: 1 }`. Key handling LayerTreeItem.tsx:140-165: Enter/' ' -> onSelect; F2 -> onStartEditing guarded by `!isLocked`; ArrowRight/Left -> onToggleExpand; ArrowDown/Up -> `onSelect(nextId, {})` computed from getVisibleLayerIds().indexOf(layer.id) with no focus move. Delete: shared/constants/commands.ts:147 `[COMMANDS.DELETE]: "Backspace"`; engine/commands/CommandCenter.ts:229 `return !target.closest(WIDGET_ROLES)` with WIDGET_ROLES including 'tree' at :28; the container carries role="tree" at index.tsx:429.
edit: Add 'Layers · keyboard focus' cloned from 142:2: one row focused-but-not-selected (2px accent inset ring, no tint, no left bar), one row focused AND selected (ring over the tint + 2px bar). Caption (clone 155:30, 280x54): 'Rows are tabbable. Enter selects, F2 renames, ←/→ collapse and expand. ↑/↓ SELECT the neighbour — they do not move focus. Delete does nothing here: bare-key commands are suppressed inside role="tree"; right-click is the only delete from the tree.'

claim: 143:237 is the locked state and, per W-M-18, is visually identical to 142:2 — same rows, same amber 🔒 on every row, same selection. It shows nothing about what a lock does off-panel.
truth: Beyond W-M-18's in-row consequences, a lock changes the CANVAS, and no board in this module or in section 09 draws it: a locked element gets a 2px dotted outline in a raw hex that is in no token (#f38ba8, a pink), cursor:not-allowed, and user-select:none — and clicking it raises a toast that names this panel by name. That toast is the only place the product tells a user where to go, and it is on no board.
evidence: editor/canvas/Canvas.css:240-249 `[data-buildrick-id][data-locked="true"] { outline: 2px dotted #f38ba8; cursor: not-allowed !important; user-select: none }` plus a selected-state variant. editor/canvas/hooks/useSelectionBehavior.ts:88-95, :106-113, :134-141 — three separate paths each `addToast({ description: "This element is locked. Unlock it in the Layers panel.", tone: "info", duration: 2500 })` and return without selecting. The lock reaches the engine at useLayerActions.ts:161-168 (`setLocked`) and the DOM attribute at the same lines.
edit: Add the canvas half to 143:237 as a side-by-side or a companion board: the element outlined 2px dotted with the not-allowed cursor, and the toast 'This element is locked. Unlock it in the Layers panel.' Pick a token for the outline in the same pass — #f38ba8 is a raw hex in no palette (DESIGN.md §Color) and this is the one place a designer would go to choose it.

claim: The right-click menu draws nine items: Cut, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete, Rename, Group selection, [not-implemented] Move to page…, Copy link.
truth: Eight of the nine ship (W-M-04/27 have the wiring). The item that is missing from BOTH the board and the menu is the inverse of one that is on both: Group selection exists, Ungroup does not. The engine has ungroupElement, the command registry binds it to Mod+Shift+G, and the Layers panel's action union does not contain the word — so a container created by the panel's own Group button can only be dissolved from the canvas menu or a keyboard chord the panel never mentions.
evidence: Engine: engine/elements/ElementManager.ts:237-251 ungroupElement (dissolves in place, refusal branches covered by engine/elements/__tests__/ElementManager.crud.test.ts:464-481); engine/commands/defaultCommands.ts:114-115 id 'ungroup' label 'Ungroup'; shared/constants/commands.ts:56 UNGROUP and :182 `[COMMANDS.UNGROUP]: "Mod+Shift+G"`. Panel: types.ts:81-96 LayerAction has cut|copy|copyLink|paste|rename|duplicate|hide|show|lock|unlock|delete|group|selectChildren|moveToTop|moveToBottom — no ungroup; components/LayerContextMenu.tsx:61-101 renders eight items; useLayerContextActions.ts:18-107 has no ungroup case. `grep -rni ungroup` over editor/panels/layers -> zero hits.
edit: Add an 'Ungroup' row to 1082:4527 directly under 'Group selection', and label its layer '[not-implemented]' exactly the way 'Move to page…' (1082:4583) already is, with no reaction. That makes the asymmetry a recorded decision instead of an oversight, and gives the eventual build a target. Note in the caption that the canvas menu and Mod+Shift+G do have it.

claim: Multi-select's headline action, per W-M-01's fix, is a four-button bulk bar whose first button is Group.
truth: Group from the Layers banner is a SECOND implementation of grouping that skips the refusal the engine's own version enforces. The engine's groupElements requires all ids to share one parent and re-sorts them into document order before wrapping. The panel's groupLayers does neither: it takes the first id's parent as the destination, ignores where the others live, and moves them in Set-iteration order — which for a ⌘-click multi-select is CLICK order. Selecting a header row and a footer row and pressing Group silently re-parents the footer into the header's section, and the canvas's Group button on the identical selection refuses.
evidence: Panel: useLayerActions.ts:268-287 groupLayers — `const parent = firstEl?.getParent?.(); if (!parent) return;` then `createElement('container')`, moveElement(group,parentId,insertIndex), then `ids.forEach(id => moveElement(id, group.getId(), group.getChildCount()))` — no same-parent test, no ordering. Engine: ElementManager.ts:210-231 groupElements — `if (!els.every(e => e.getParent()?.getId() === parentId)) return null;` at :221 and an indexOf sort at :223-226. The engine version is what the canvas menu (editor/canvas/menus/actions/standaloneActions.ts:79) and the 'group' command (engine/commands/defaultCommands.ts:108) call. The banner's Group is wired at index.tsx:316-318 -> LayerSelectionBanner.tsx:37-44.
edit: On 143:295, draw the multi-select with all three rows under ONE parent (a Section and two of its children), so the board does not teach the cross-parent selection the panel mishandles; and add to the bulk-bar caption: 'Group wraps the selection in a new container at the first row's position. It is only defined for siblings — the canvas refuses a cross-parent group and this panel does not.' If the design intends cross-parent grouping, a refusal state has to be drawn, because today the two entry points disagree.

claim: Nothing on 143:179 or 155:29 says whether hiding can be undone, and the eye's own copy promises only that the element still publishes.
truth: A hide cannot be undone. toggleVisibility mutates a React Set and writes a DOM attribute — no transaction is opened, so ⌘Z steps over it entirely and lands on whatever document edit came before. The event that was designed to carry the undo, LAYER_VISIBILITY_TOGGLED, is declared with an `undo: () => void` in its payload type and is emitted by nothing and listened to by nothing. Same for lock. The state itself lives per-browser in localStorage, so it is invisible to a collaborator and gone on a different machine (W-M-15 records the rename half of the same store).
evidence: useLayerActions.ts:127-137 toggleVisibility — setHiddenIds only, no composer.beginTransaction (contrast :211-213 deleteLayer, :222-224 duplicateLayer, :235-237 moveToTop, which all open one); :140-146 the DOM write. shared/constants/events.ts:78 `LAYER_VISIBILITY_TOGGLED: "layer:visibility-toggled"` and :822 `[EVENTS.LAYER_VISIBILITY_TOGGLED]: { id: string; hidden: boolean; undo: () => void }`; grep for both the constant and the string 'layer:visibility' across src -> those two declaration lines and nothing else; findings/EVENT-GRAPH.json lists LAYER_VISIBILITY_TOGGLED under 'never' (declared, never named). Storage: layersPersistence.ts:15-22 keys 'buildrick-layers-<pageId>-{hidden,locked,names}' in localStorage.
edit: Add to caption 155:29: 'Dimming is not undoable — ⌘Z skips it — and it is stored in this browser only, so a collaborator does not see it.' If that is not the intended contract, this is the board where the toast-with-Undo (the canvas delete already ships one) gets designed; clone the pattern from the canvas delete toast named in W-M-14.

claim: The section draws the canvas→tree direction (1082:4835 is the scroll case, and W-M-21 asks for the 'revealed' arrival board) and says nothing about the tree→canvas direction.
truth: The two directions are not symmetric, and the asymmetry is the one that costs a user. Canvas→tree is fully wired: hovering the canvas emits CANVAS_HOVER, the shell stores it, the tree auto-expands every ancestor and highlights the row; 'Show in Layers' switches tab, opens the drawer and scrolls the row into view. Tree→canvas stops at selection: clicking a row calls composer.selection.select and nothing scrolls, zooms or pans the canvas to it. On a long page, selecting a footer row from the top of the tree changes the inspector and leaves the viewport where it was, with no element visible anywhere.
evidence: Canvas→tree: Canvas.tsx:437-441 emits EVENTS.CANVAS_HOVER; StudioPanels.tsx:311-320 stores it as canvasHoveredId; TabRouter.tsx:149 -> LayersTab.tsx:200 -> useLayerTree.ts:167-183 auto-expands ancestors; LayerTreeItem.tsx:91,130 paints `.bdc-canvas-hover`. Reveal: standaloneActions.ts:42-46 emits EVENTS.SHOW_IN_LAYERS -> useEditorEventListeners.ts:111-127 switches tab, opens the drawer, emits EVENTS.LAYERS_SCROLL_TO_SELECTION -> index.tsx:209-216 -> scrollToSelection (:181-187). Tree→canvas: useLayerSelection.ts:68-75 selectSingle -> composer.selection.select(el) and stops. The only scrollIntoView on the canvas is inside the zoom-to-fit callback (Canvas.tsx:335-350) and the deep-link path (shell/hooks/useDeepLink.ts:44); neither is on the selection path. Tree→canvas HOVER does work, by direct DOM class (useLayerSelection.ts:117-129 adds 'bd-layer-hover-highlight') plus EVENTS.LAYER_HOVER (LayersTab.tsx:130-135 -> useCanvasHover.ts:53-70).
edit: Add 'Layers · select → canvas' cloned from 142:2, drawn as a two-pane frame (tree at 280 + a canvas thumbnail): a deep row selected in the tree with the canvas viewport UNCHANGED and the selected element off-screen, and a caption stating the rule: 'Selecting a row selects the element. It does not move the canvas — the reverse trip (Show in Layers) does scroll the tree.' That is the decision this board exists to force.

claim: 'Copy link' is a plain row on 1082:4527 with no consequence drawn.
truth: It is the only Layers action that produces a toast, and it produces two — a success and a failure — with copy that no board carries. It also writes two query params, and the reason for the second one is a real constraint worth drawing: the element registry only holds the ACTIVE page, so the link must carry the page id or the consumer cannot resolve the element.
evidence: useLayerContextActions.ts:28-43 — builds `new URL(window.location.href)` with `el=<nodeId>` and `page=<activePageId>`, then `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...).then(success, failure)` with addToast({ description: 'Link copied — opens the editor with this element selected', tone: 'success' }) and addToast({ description: "Couldn't copy the link", tone: 'error' }). The page-id rationale is recorded at :29-33.
edit: Add a small consequence board or an overlay on 1082:4527 showing both toasts with their exact strings, and note on the caption that the link is `?el=<id>&page=<id>` and reopens the editor with the element selected. Toasts live in section 20 · Notifications; either cross-reference it or draw them here — but do not leave the module's only shareable output undrawn.

claim: 143:355 is self-labelled UNBUILDABLE on the grounds that buildLayersFromEngine always emits a root row, so layers.length===0 means no page/composer. Caption 155:32 reads only 'Copy from shell §5.7.'
truth: The manifest note and W-M-24 are right and still one step too generous. With no composer the empty state cannot appear either, because the tab renders the loading skeleton instead: the body is gated on `composer && !projectLoading`. So LayersEmptyState is reachable in exactly one situation — composer exists, loading has finished, and there is no active page or the active page has no root element — and its copy ('This page is empty. Drop something on the canvas to see it here.') describes a different situation entirely.
evidence: LayersTab.tsx:194-210 — `{composer && !projectLoading ? (<LayersTreeBoundary><LayersPanel .../></LayersTreeBoundary>) : (<LayersLoadingSkeleton />)}`, with the reason for reading projectLoading rather than composer recorded at :187-193. useLayerTree.ts:58-72 returns [] only for !composer / !page / !rootElement, and :97 `setLayers([buildTree(rootElement, 0)])` otherwise. index.tsx:431 `{state.layers.length === 0 && <LayersEmptyState .../>}`; LayersEmptyState.tsx:20-22 carries the copy. Prior: W-M-24, D-F-22.
edit: Rename 143:355 to 'Layers · no page open' and replace its two lines with copy that matches the reachable state ('No page open. Pick a page to see its structure.'), or exclude the page root from the tree so the drawn state becomes reachable and keep the current copy. Replace caption 155:32's 'Copy from shell §5.7' with the copy the component actually ships, whichever way that lands — a caption that points at another document is not a spec.

claim: Caption 788:4303 reads: 'Tree fetching. Toolbar and the layer count stay put, because both are chrome the user can act on before data lands.'
truth: Half right and the wrong half is load-bearing. The toolbar does stay, and it cannot be acted on: the search box is a controlled input whose value is only consumed by the panel that is not mounted yet, and ⊞ / ⊟ emit into a listener that mounts with the panel. The count also stays, and it reads '0 layers' — the board draws '12 layers' (W-M-23). The tab's own code states the rule the caption violates, in the failure case: 'a count of a list that did not load is not a fact.'
evidence: LayersTab.tsx:159-185 the toolbar sits outside the loading conditional; its ⊞/⊟ handlers emit 'layers:expand-all'/'layers:collapse-all' (:137-143) whose only listeners are registered by LayersPanel (index.tsx:49-59), which is not mounted while loading. The footer at :216-222 renders `${stats.total} layer(s)` from a stats state initialised to `{ total: 0, selected: 0 }` (:113) and only updated by the panel's emit (index.tsx:64-67). The failure-case rule is at :212-215. Prior: W-M-23.
edit: Replace 788:4303's text with: 'Tree fetching. The toolbar stays for position, not for use — its controls talk to the panel that has not mounted. The count is a skeleton, not a number: a count of a list that has not loaded is not a fact.' Then apply W-M-23's fix to 775:4130 (drop the '12 layers', draw a skeleton bar in the footer).

claim: 'Selectable in the tree, not on canvas. The tree is the only way back to a locked element — clicking the canvas cannot reach it.'
truth: Correct, and correct in an unobvious way that is worth leaving alone. All three canvas selection paths test isLocked() and return without selecting; the tree's own row click has no lock guard at all, so the tree really is the only way back. Checked, no edit.
evidence: editor/canvas/hooks/useSelectionBehavior.ts:88-95 (click-through first hit), :106-113 (click-through cycling), :134-141 (normal selection) — each `if (element.isLocked()) { addToast(…); return; }`. LayerTreeItem.tsx:188-190 onClick -> onSelect with no lock test; useLayerSelection.ts:68-75 selectSingle -> composer.selection.select unconditionally. The one thing a locked row does lose in the tree is drag and rename (LayerTreeItem.tsx:99, :146, :196) — already covered by W-M-18.
edit: No change.

claim: 'Accent tint + 2px left bar per row; the inspector switches to the batch panel.'
truth: Both halves verified. The selected row is `background: var(--bk-accent-tint)` with a 2px accent bar drawn as a ::before pinned to the left edge, and the inspector does swap to a multi-select toolbar above one element.
evidence: layers-v2.css:40-55 `.bdc-lr.bdc-sel { background: var(--bk-accent-tint) }` and `.bdc-lr.bdc-sel::before { position:absolute; left:0; top:0; bottom:0; width:2px; background: var(--bk-accent) }`. editor/inspector/ProInspector.tsx:298 `const hasMultipleSelected = selectedIds.length > 1 || isMultiSelect;` -> :302 renders MultiSelectToolbar (imported :33). Selection itself mirrors the composer, so tree and canvas cannot disagree (useLayerSelection.ts:44-66 syncs on ELEMENT_SELECTED, SELECTION_MULTIPLE, SELECTION_CLEARED, SELECTION_ADDED, SELECTION_REMOVED).

target: 1776:8375 / 142:2  (row fields — the M / T breakpoint badges)
claim: No Layers board draws a per-row breakpoint badge.
truth: The board is right and the CODE is the one carrying a ghost. LayerTreeItem renders 14x14 'M' and 'T' badges from `layer.breakpointOverrides`, and nothing ever writes that field: the only two places a LayerItem is constructed are buildTree, which sets id/type/tagName/depth/preview/children and no overrides, and the flat-search spread, which copies whatever buildTree produced. The badges are unreachable, so there is nothing for the board to draw. Filed as coverage, and flagged for the coordinator as a code-side dead field — not a Figma edit.
evidence: LayerTreeItem.tsx:276-281 renders `{layer.breakpointOverrides?.mobile?.hidden && …}` / `?.tablet?.hidden`, styled at layers-v2.css:133-143. types.ts:49 declares the field optional. `grep -rn breakpointOverrides src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` -> exactly five hits: ProInspector.tsx:165,170 (a different, real thing — useBreakpointOverrides), types.ts:49, LayerTreeItem.tsx:276,279. useLayerTree.ts:88-95 buildTree writes six keys, none of them breakpointOverrides; index.tsx:353 spreads `{...it, children: [], depth: 0}`. Same for LayerItem.isHidden / isLocked / customName (types.ts:39-41) — declared, never written; the real state lives in the hiddenIds / lockedIds Sets and the customNames Map.

claim: W-M-02 reports that the reorder the board draws is not the reorder the code performs — the drop index is decremented twice.
truth: Re-verified independently, unchanged, and it is the module's most serious functional defect: the panel subtracts one for a same-parent forward move and the engine subtracts one again for the same case, so [A,B,C] dropping A after B calls moveElement(A, root, 1), which the engine adjusts to 0, and the order does not change. Recording the confirmation rather than re-filing; W-M-02 owns the fix and W-M-03 owns the missing drop-inside board.
evidence: index.tsx:155-166 — `let dropIndex = position === 'before' ? targetIndex : targetIndex + 1;` then `if (sourceParent && sourceParent.getId() === parent.getId()) { const sourceIndex = parent.getChildIndex(sourceEl); if (sourceIndex < dropIndex) dropIndex -= 1; }`. engine/elements/manager/ElementCRUD.ts:180-190 — `if (movingWithinSameParent && adjustedIndex !== undefined) { const oldIndex = oldParent.getChildIndex(element); if (oldIndex > -1 && oldIndex < adjustedIndex) adjustedIndex = Math.max(0, adjustedIndex - 1); }`. Prior: W-M-02, and MOD-D covers engine/drag.
